title: The Old Stand
text: A stand of huge, straight trees, perfect timber, taller than any tower, their bark silver and smooth. A ring of standing stones surrounds them, each one carved with a face. The faces are all frowning, and none of the stones are mossy.

options.label: Fell the silver trees. Timber like this would raise towers at home.

outcomes.text: Fine timber, a great deal of it, and the stone faces frown harder.
The stones were guarding the trees, and they still are.

options.label: The wisest asks the stones' leave first, as the old folk would have.

outcomes.text: One tree, given freely, and the stone faces ease.

options.label: Take only the fallen wood, and leave the stones nothing to frown at.

outcomes.text: Less, but no one minds, and no stone turns to watch you go.
